scope: Pulse containers and their external flows
method: STRIDE per element and per boundary-crossing flow

threats.title: Forged or replayed bearer token
threats.description: Every API route trusts the Authorization header. A token minted with a stolen signing key, or replayed after logout, grants full workspace access.
threats.mitigation: Auth Middleware verifies RS256 signatures against Auth0's JWKS, checks audience and expiry, and tokens live 15 minutes.

threats.title: Channel ids are not checked against membership
threats.description: Messages Controller loads a channel by id from the path. A member of one workspace can post to any channel whose id they guess.
threats.mitigation: Resolve membership in Auth Middleware and reject requests for channels outside the caller's workspaces.

threats.title: WebSocket subscriptions are not re-authorised
threats.description: Real-time Service validates the token at connect time only. A user removed from a channel keeps receiving its messages until they reconnect.
threats.mitigation: Re-check membership on each fan-out, or drop subscriptions when a membership-removed event arrives.

threats.title: Unbounded connections per user
threats.description: Nothing limits how many sockets one account can hold open. A script can exhaust the instance's file descriptors.
threats.mitigation: Cap connections per user and per IP; close idle sockets after a timeout.

threats.title: Spoofed events on the queue
threats.description: Anything that can write to the SQS queue can inject a message that every subscriber sees as genuine.
threats.mitigation: Only the API's instance role has sqs:SendMessage; the queue policy denies all other principals.

threats.title: Message edits are not audited
threats.description: Editing or deleting a message overwrites the row. There is no record of who changed what.
threats.mitigation: Accepted for now: product does not expose edit history. Revisit if compliance customers ask.

threats.title: Messages stored in plaintext across two regions
threats.description: API Database replicates to us-east-1 with default encryption only. Anyone with read access to either table reads every message.
threats.mitigation: Use a customer-managed KMS key per environment and restrict table read to the API and Real-time roles.

threats.title: Login redirect to a look-alike identity provider
threats.description: If the OIDC redirect were attacker-controlled, the browser would hand the authorisation code to the wrong party.
threats.mitigation: Auth0 only honours the allow-listed callback URL; the SPA uses PKCE so a captured code is useless without the verifier.

threats.title: Invite spam burns the SES sending quota
threats.description: The invite endpoint sends one email per call with no limit, so a user can exhaust the daily quota and block real invites.
threats.mitigation: Rate-limit invites per workspace per hour.
